project.name: PromptForge
project.summary: Reshapes any rough prompt into a best-practice prompt: a quality score, the gaps found, a ready-to-paste rewrite, a fill-in-the-blank template, and the clarifying questions still open.

serialization.notes: Spring Boot 4 ships Jackson 3; the com.fasterxml.jackson.databind packages are not on the classpath.

architectureStyle.name: layered-hexagonal-core
architectureStyle.description: A pure, framework-free analysis core surrounded by adapters. The core has no Spring imports and no I/O, so it is deterministic, fast to test, and portable to another stack.
architectureStyle.dependencyRule: web -> service -> core; llm <- service; core depends on nothing but the JDK and its own model package.

layers.name: Presentation
layers.responsibility: HTTP contract, request validation, JSON error shaping, and the single-page UI.

layers.name: Application
layers.responsibility: Orchestrates the pipeline: analyse -> rewrite -> (optional) LLM upgrade -> fallback. Owns the engine-selection policy.

layers.name: Domain
layers.responsibility: The prompt anatomy, the scoring model, the diagnostics catalogue, the rewrite rules and the output templates.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.responsibility: Outbound calls to LLM providers plus the configuration that enables them.

components.name: PromptForgeApplication
components.responsibility: Entry point. Boots the context and enables configuration-properties scanning.

components.name: PromptAnalyzer
components.responsibility: Reads the prompt, detects role, task, audience, stack, goal, constraints, format and examples, scores the seven anatomy dimensions and produces ordered diagnostics.

components.name: PromptRewriter
components.responsibility: Builds the reshaped prompt, the placeholder template and the clarifying questions from an analysis.

components.name: PromptTemplates
components.responsibility: Default role, output format, acceptance criteria and constraints per task type.

components.name: DomainLexicon
components.responsibility: Vocabulary: domain-to-role map, task-type keywords, action verbs, unmeasurable words, conflicting term pairs.

components.name: TextUtil
components.responsibility: Sentence and clause splitting, sentence casing, bullet stripping.

components.name: Domain model
components.responsibility: Dimension, Severity, TaskType, PromptProfile, Engine, Diagnostic, DimensionScore, PromptAnalysis, PromptRequest, PromptResult.

components.name: PromptReshapeService
components.responsibility: Runs the rule engine, then optionally upgrades the rewrite with an LLM that is grounded in the analyzer findings. Falls back to the rule result on any provider failure.

components.name: LlmGateway
components.responsibility: Resolves the provider to use (explicit override, configured preference, or auto-detect) and reports which providers have a usable key.

components.name: LlmProperties
components.responsibility: Binds promptforge.llm.* - provider preference, per-provider key and model, max tokens, timeout.

components.name: AnthropicLlmClient
components.responsibility: Calls the Anthropic Messages API and concatenates the text content blocks.

components.name: OpenAiLlmClient
components.responsibility: Calls the OpenAI Chat Completions API and reads choices[0].message.content.

components.name: GeminiLlmClient
components.responsibility: Calls the Gemini generateContent API with a system instruction and concatenates the candidate parts.

components.name: HttpLlmSupport
components.responsibility: Shared HTTP plumbing: JSON build/parse, status handling, timeout, safe error messages.

components.name: ApiExceptionHandler
components.responsibility: Converts validation and unexpected failures into a consistent JSON error shape.

components.name: PromptForge UI
components.responsibility: Prompt input, profile and engine controls, sample prompts, score ring, dimension bars, and the four result tabs (reshaped, template, questions, findings).

promptAnatomy.description: The seven dimensions every prompt is measured against. The score is the weighted sum, expressed 0-100.

dimensions.label: Role
dimensions.meaning: Who the AI should be: expertise and seniority.

dimensions.label: Task
dimensions.meaning: One explicit action and one named deliverable.

dimensions.label: Context
dimensions.meaning: Audience, background, stack and the goal behind the request.

dimensions.label: Output format
dimensions.meaning: The required shape of the response.

dimensions.label: Examples
dimensions.meaning: One representative sample of a good answer.

severities.label: Critical
severities.meaning: The prompt cannot produce a reliable result without this.

severities.label: Warning
severities.meaning: The result will be noticeably weaker than it could be.

severities.label: Info
severities.meaning: An improvement that is optional or stylistic.

diagnostics.title: Prompt is too short to be specific
Many different actions in one prompt
No example of a good answer
Prompt is a single dense block

errorShape.fields: optional map of field -> message (validation failures only)

endpoints.purpose: Analyse a prompt and return the reshape result.

fields.name: strict
fields.meaning: Template mode: the reshaped prompt keeps its <placeholders> instead of the filled-in defaults.

fields.name: provider
fields.meaning: Overrides the configured provider for this call.

fields.name: model
fields.meaning: Overrides the configured model id for this call.

fields.name: reshapedPrompt
fields.meaning: Complete, usable prompt with labelled defaults for the gaps.

fields.name: templatePrompt
fields.meaning: Same skeleton with <placeholders> where information is still missing.

fields.name: questions
fields.meaning: Clarifying questions that would close the remaining gaps.

fields.name: notes
fields.meaning: Engine notes, e.g. a fallback notice.

endpoints.purpose: Metadata for the UI: profiles, dimension anatomy, configured providers.

steps: PromptRewriter.rewrite(analysis, profile, includeExamples) -> reshaped + template + questions
Steps 1-2 of the rule engine run first - the analysis always happens
LlmGateway.resolve(provider, model) -> optional LlmClient; empty when no key is configured
No client -> fall back to the rule result, engineUsed = 'Rule-based (fallback)', note explains why
Client available -> the analyzer findings, task type and draft template are sent as the user message
The model answers with JSON {reshapedPrompt, questions}; the service parses it leniently (code fences tolerated)
Provider error or unparsable answer -> fall back to the rule result with an explanatory note

keyAlgorithms.name: Frame stripping
keyAlgorithms.detail: Removes greeting, 'can/could you', 'I need you to', 'I want to' and 'help me' wrappers, then strips a leftover 'you to', producing the cleaned request that the task and the quoted fallback are built from.

keyAlgorithms.name: Task extraction
keyAlgorithms.detail: The first word of the cleaned request is tested against the action-verb list; otherwise the first sentence carrying an action verb wins; a question counts as a task. When nothing qualifies, the request is quoted verbatim in the Task section so the intent is never lost.

keyAlgorithms.name: Constraint clause splitting
keyAlgorithms.detail: Commas and semicolons always break a clause. A conjunction breaks it only when both sides carry a constraint, so 'Use only Spring Boot and JPA' keeps its second half while 'it should be professional and not too long' splits into two constraints.

keyAlgorithms.name: Format detection
keyAlgorithms.detail: Most specific signal wins: an explicit phrase ('respond with a Markdown table containing ...'), then a format word in an output context ('in JSON'), then a format word next to an output verb. A bare format word is ignored, so 'our sales csv' (an input file) is not mistaken for a requested output format.

keyAlgorithms.name: Stack de-duplication
keyAlgorithms.detail: A generic token is dropped when a more specific token already covers it, so the stack reads 'Java, Spring Boot, JPA, REST' rather than 'Java, Spring Boot, Spring, JPA, REST'.

keyAlgorithms.name: Placeholder policy
keyAlgorithms.detail: The template writes known values in full and marks only real gaps with <placeholders>, so the template and the reshaped prompt never disagree about what is known. With strict=true the reshaped prompt is the template, so the caller fills the gaps instead of accepting the defaults.

configuration.secretsPolicy: No key is ever committed. Keys come from environment variables only and are read through Spring configuration properties.

testStrategy.approach: Behavioural tests over the public surface of the domain core, plus an HTTP-level test of the controller.

layers.focus: scoring, politeness stripping, contradiction detection, stack de-duplication, constraint clause extraction, format detection, example extraction
section completeness, placeholder policy, constraint carry-over, request preservation
success path, blank-prompt validation, metadata endpoint, health endpoint

engineeringPractices: Immutable records for all payloads; no setters on domain types.
Enums carry behaviour-adjacent data (weights, labels, defaults) instead of scattering magic numbers.
Regexes are named constants, never inlined literals.
Every diagnostic carries a prompt-specific suggestion, not generic advice.
The LLM path is strictly additive: no provider call can break a request.

deployment.notes: Single stateless process. No database, no session state, no migration step.

nonFunctionalSummary.determinism: The rule engine returns the same output for the same input, on every platform.
nonFunctionalSummary.offlineCapability: Full functionality with no API key and no network access.
nonFunctionalSummary.latency: Local analysis is single-pass regex work over the prompt; no I/O on the RULE path.
nonFunctionalSummary.privacy: Prompt content never leaves the machine unless the caller explicitly selects the LLM engine.
nonFunctionalSummary.resilience: Provider outage or malformed provider output degrades to the local engine with a note.
